office_does: The sheriff runs county law enforcement and the county jail, and in Grays Harbor also oversees emergency management and court security.
race_blurb: First-term Sheriff Darrin Wallace, who led the primary about 60% to 40%, faces Ed Welter, a detective in his office and the mayor of Westport; neither states a party preference. Wallace is running on falling crime figures and a new criminal justice center, and Welter on public engagement and adding deputies.

candidates.summary: Incumbent sheriff since 2023 with 20 years in the sheriff's office and 20 in the Coast Guard, running on falling crime figures and a new jail.
highlights: Calls a new criminal justice center his #1 priority; says modular units could cut its estimated cost to about $50 million [S1][S4]
Says he has been 'tough on crime' and will keep aggressively investigating and arresting offenders [S1]
Will keep funding a sheriff's position on the Drug Task Force [S4]
Said at a July forum he would retire once the new jail was under contract, then pledged to serve the full four years [S5]

experience.basis: Incumbent sheriff with 20 years in the office who runs on his first-term record.

safety.basis: Enforcement framing ('tough on crime', aggressive investigation and arrests, Drug Task Force); treatment appears only as expanded rehabilitation services in a new jail.

spending.basis: Pushes a roughly $50 million jail (grant, bond or partnership) while stressing he stayed under budget and halved the estimated jail cost.

candidates.summary: Sheriff's office detective and mayor of Westport, running on public engagement, more deputies and working with state legislators.
highlights: Says staffing has stayed flat since 2000 while the unincorporated population grew almost 30% [S4]
Says all crimes, including property crime, should be 'investigated to their fullest' [S4]
Backs therapeutic courts as part of accountability, provided cases carry enough consequences [S6]
Would attend public meetings countywide and seek regular updates on the commissioners' agenda [S4]

experience.basis: Detective with about 12 years in law enforcement and a sitting mayor, never in county office, who pitches 'a new perspective.'

safety.basis: Enforce all laws and fully investigate property crime, with proactive drug enforcement; therapeutic courts and community policing alongside.

spending.basis: Argues for more deputies and better facilities as population grows, while acknowledging budget constraints.
